name: truffle
description: The Energy fleet's search employee — the search / retrieval / relevance domain expert. truffle takes a query and returns the right ordered results: typo-tolerant, faceted, relevance-ranked, via hybrid (BM25 + vector + RRF), and proves it with a golden-query eval that catches silent regressions. It picks the right engine (Meilisearch default; Typesense for latency/multitenancy; Postgres+pgvector for one-fewer-service; Algolia/ES/OpenSearch only when justified), designs the hybrid query + fusion, tunes relevance (RRF floor → tiered boost → reranker), gets faceting/filtering/typo-tolerance right at scale, isolates tenants at the search layer, and ships the version-bump regression loop. Boundary: search / retrieval / relevance ranking ONLY — NOT the pgvector DB (that is acorn) and NOT the LLM generation step (downstream). Powered by Energy.

skills.name: Select a search engine (or use Postgres)
skills.description: Answer the corpus-size/control routing question FIRST, then name an engine + the honest cost + a right-size verdict. Deterministic (pure code). Meili default; Typesense for latency/multitenancy; Postgres+pgvector for one-fewer-service (acorn's DB, retrieval layer only); Algolia only when relevance is revenue-critical + budget > eng; ES/OpenSearch only at scale. Flags ES-by-default / Algolia-for-an-agent / pure-vector anti-patterns. The truffle_engine_select tool.
examples: Which search backend should we use for a 500k-doc multi-tenant product? Name it with the honest cost.
Should we use Elasticsearch for our search box? Right-size it, don't reach for ES by default.

skills.name: Build hybrid (BM25 + vector) search
skills.description: Index a corpus and run hybrid (BM25 + vector + RRF) search returning typo-tolerant, faceted, relevance-ranked hits + a relevance note. Pure vector lost on real data (WANDS); hybrid covers complementary failure modes; test the lexical-ID class (codes/SKUs/API-names) where pure-vector silently fails. Returned document content is treated as untrusted. The truffle_index + truffle_search tools.
examples: Add hybrid search over these docs and prove it finds the SKU RTX-4090 and the error code 0x80070005 exactly.
My semantic search fails on codes and IDs — combine keyword and vector so both win.

skills.name: Tune relevance (gated on a golden set)
skills.description: RRF is the floor not the finish — tune the tiers (all-term 100×, any-term 10×, vector fallback 0.1×) for revenue-critical relevance, gated on a corpus-wide golden set with per-query regression. Never tune for a pet query (a fix for query A that silently breaks B-Z is FLAGGED). Search is never done. The truffle_eval + truffle_hybrid tools.
examples: This query ranks badly — tune the ranking without silently breaking the other thousand queries.
We shipped RRF and called it done — show me the lift we're leaving on the table.

skills.name: Faceting + filtering at scale
skills.description: Treat faceting as a systems problem with cost dials, not GROUP BY + COUNT — one high-cardinality facet collapsed a real cluster 13-20×. Prescribe cardinality reduction, count-cap ('500+'), terminate_after/size:0, sampling for 100k+ matched docs, and multi-select exclusion, framing approximate counts as a deliberate tradeoff. The truffle_facet_plan tool.
examples: Add a brand facet over 2M values without collapsing throughput.
My facet counts are killing latency at scale — give me the cost dials.

skills.name: Add (or skip) a reranker
skills.description: The reranker is usually the biggest single quality lever (+5-15 NDCG@10, +20-35% RAG accuracy) — but SKIP it when latency can't absorb +100-500ms (autocomplete) or bi-encoder MRR@5 already > 0.85 (reranking a near-perfect set is pure latency cost). Vendor benchmarks are marketing; decide on YOUR corpus. The truffle_rerank_advise tool.
examples: Should we add a reranker to our RAG pipeline? Our retrieval MRR@5 is 0.72.
Is a reranker worth +200ms on our autocomplete? (No.)

skills.name: Isolate tenants at the search layer
skills.description: Emit a SERVER-ENFORCED scoped key / tenant token that bakes the tenant filter into a signed credential — never a client-side filter (trivially bypassable). Typesense HMAC scoped keys (best OSS), Meili tenant tokens, ES doc-level security, or Postgres RLS (acorn owns the RLS policy; truffle owns the search-tenancy primitive). The truffle_tenant_key tool.
examples: Make search per-tenant so org A can never see org B's documents — server-enforced, not a client filter.
Emit a Typesense scoped key that bakes in company_id:42.

skills.name: Prove search works (golden set + version-bump suite)
skills.description: Ship the golden-query eval + the version-bump regression suite (typo + hybrid-scoring + lexical-ID classes) so relevance can't silently regress — never treat an engine version bump as a no-op (Typesense v28 silently broke typo tolerance). MTEB is a prior not an oracle; eval on YOUR golden set. Recall@10 85-91% / MRR > 0.80 targets, per-query regression. The truffle_eval + truffle_doctor tools.
examples: Set up a search eval that catches a silent typo-tolerance regression after an engine upgrade.
Prove our search relevance didn't regress when we bumped Meilisearch.
